signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy Divergence
signals.text: NZD/CHF trades with a severe downside bias as broad G10 scorecard performance exposes acute weakness in the kiwi against the outperforming franc. The 1W G10 strength scorecard identifies CHF as the top leader (+0.625% avg across 6 pairs) while NZD is the primary laggard (-0.462% avg across 4 pairs), creating a 1.087% bilateral spread. This divergence is reinforced by underlying economic data, where Switzerland's Economic Surprise Index stands at +28.0 (strong positive) while New Zealand's index registers at -15.4 (strong negative). Headlining central bank guidance adds fundamental fuel as SNB Vice President Martin signaled inflation risks reaching 1.5% and brought December rate hikes into view. Meanwhile, RBNZ holds policy at 2.75% against a deteriorating domestic macro background. Technical structures remain heavy for the kiwi, with NZD/USD trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.5479 while USD/CHF holds at 0.8376. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/CHF, exploiting institutional G10 bilateral divergence and data divergence. Catalyst: SNB policy meeting 10 Dec — rate hike guidance in focus. Risk: RBNZ delivers an unexpected hawkish policy pivot that invalidates the relative weakness theme.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Volatility Regime + Carry vs Correlation Break
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.962, anchored between its 20-day SMA at 158.62 and the 200-day SMA at 158.85 following a wide-range bearish engulfing bar. The SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential of +268bp continues to favor USD holding long positions, but cross-asset correlations display severe structural distortion. The USD/JPY correlation with VIX sits at -0.054 versus its 252-day norm of +0.266 (z = -2.24σ), showing JPY carry positions failing to unwind despite broad equity stress and VIX spiking to 35.9. USD/JPY 1M implied volatility sits at 7.5% against a 30-day realized volatility of 5.5%, generating a +2.0% Vol Risk Premium that reflects heightened options market caution. Options positioning shows 25-delta Risk Reversals at -1.77, indicating aggressive institutional hedging for downside JPY strength. Traders should monitor the 160.00 intervention watch level where Japanese official defense historically intensifies. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY, balancing +268bp OIS carry against extreme options downside skew. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release on 05:00 UTC 23 Nov. Risk: VIX surges further above 35.0 and forces a rapid liquidation of crowded JPY shorts.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Extreme + OIS Carry Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.43140, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.4140, SMA50 at 1.4131, SMA200 at 1.3929) within an established technical uptrend. OIS carry differentials favor the greenback, with SOFR at 3.91% versus CORRA at 2.55%, providing a +136bp baseline support for USD long positions. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds hold a net short position of -75,447 contracts in CAD (37th percentile of its 52-week range), confirming institutional alignment with the trend. However, retail sentiment has reached an extreme imbalance, with Retail sentiment data community data logging 92% of retail traders short USD/CAD and only 8% long. This extreme retail short positioning diverges directly from institutional positioning and rate fundamentals, creating significant contrarian squeeze risk if price breaks further higher. BEER fair value model flags spot as rich (z = +1.90σ vs fair value 1.4248), suggesting long-term valuation resistance. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by OIS carry advantage and contrarian retail squeeze potential. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem Speech at 23:19 UTC. Risk: BoC signals a pause in rate cuts, narrowing the +136bp OIS yield advantage.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Position Stalling + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.66550, pinned firmly below its technical moving average cluster with SMA20 at 0.6883, SMA50 at 0.6964, and SMA200 at 0.7046. CFTC data for week ending Nov 17 shows Leveraged Funds hold net long positions of +26,143 contracts, but the weekly delta of -15,052 contracts marks a sharp stalling in institutional buying (52-week percentile falling to 19). The RBA holds rates at 4.85% against the Fed at 4.00%, offering a -94bp OIS carry advantage to AUD, yet spot price fails to capitalize due to deteriorating domestic activity. Australia's flash PMI sank to 46.1, marking the fastest private sector contraction in 5 years and capping RBA rate hike expectations. Options markets reflect downside hedging with 25-delta Risk Reversals printing -1.43 (put skew). Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, macro weakness breaking down technical support despite carry advantage. Catalyst: Australia Construction Work Done data at 00:30 UTC. Risk: Australia Flash PMI recovers rapidly, forcing a rebuild of speculative AUD long positions.
